questions.question: Bholanath Singh was the leader of which of the following revolts?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Bholanath Singh** was a prominent leader of the **Tamar Revolt**, which took place in the region of **Jharkhand**.
 
• The Tamar Revolt occurred during the early 19th century, specifically in the **year 1789** against the oppressive practices of landlords and the British East India Company.
 
• The revolt was largely driven by tribal communities, including the **Munda tribes**, who resisted exploitative policies and forced taxation.
 
• Bholanath Singh played a crucial role in organizing the tribal groups and leading them in their fight against exploitation and injustice.
 
• The Tamar Revolt was one of the early tribal revolts in India, showcasing the resistance of indigenous communities against colonial rule and feudal oppression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tribal Revolts in India:**

 
 
• Tribal revolts like the **Santhal Revolt (1855-56)**, the **Kol Revolt (1831)**, and the **Munda Revolt (1899-1900)** were significant uprisings against colonial exploitation and local feudal systems.
 
• These revolts were characterized by the resistance of tribal communities against policies that disrupted their traditional ways of life.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Colonial Policies:**
 
 
• The British introduced land revenue policies that marginalized tribal communities and forced them into bonded labor and economic exploitation.
 
• These policies led to widespread resentment among tribal groups, culminating in revolts like the Tamar Revolt.
 
 
 
• **Leadership in Tribal Movements:**
 
 
• Tribal leaders like Bholanath Singh and others such as **Birsa Munda** played a crucial role in organizing resistance against colonial and feudal systems.
 
• Their leadership was instrumental in galvanizing tribal communities to fight for their rights and preserve their cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Tribal Resistance:**
 
 
• Tribal uprisings like the Tamar Revolt are considered important milestones in the history of India's fight against colonial oppression.
 
• They laid the foundation for later movements that emphasized social justice and the rights of indigenous communities.

• Cases like civil disputes, matrimonial disputes, labor disputes, and compoundable criminal cases are usually resolved by Lok Adalats.

• It establishes State and District Legal Services Authorities to oversee the implementation of legal aid and Lok Adalats.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Lok Adalat:**
 
 
• Eliminates the lengthy process of litigation and provides speedy justice.
 
• Reduces the burden on regular courts and saves resources.

questions.question: Akash sold an article at a loss of 21%. If he had bought the item at 8% less and had sold it for ₹198 more, then he would have gained 5%. Find the cost price (in ₹) of the article.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Initial CP** be 100 units. Initial SP at 21% loss = 79 units.

New CP (8% less) = 92 units. New SP at 5% gain = 92 × 1.05 = 96.6 units.

Difference in SP = 96.6 − 79 = 17.6 units.

Given 17.6 units = ₹198. Therefore, 1 unit = 198 ÷ 17.6 = 11.25.

Initial CP = 100 × 11.25 = ₹1125.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial loss = 21%, New CP = 0.92 × Initial CP, Price increase = ₹198, Final gain = 5%.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 ± P/L)% | CP = Initial cost of the article.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a26fd7387f3162193d97d30fd8bbd7c13d75c67207561e22a249050420961f8f.png] 

⇒ Let CP = x. Initial SP = 0.79x.

⇒ New CP = 0.92x. New SP = 0.92x × (1.05) = 0.966x.

⇒ According to the question: 0.966x − 0.79x = 198.

⇒ 0.176x = 198.

⇒ x = 198 ÷ 0.176 = 1125.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change in Profit

When both CP and SP change, the **resultant profit percentage** is calculated on the **new CP**, not the original one.

Unitary Method Application

In profit and loss word problems, assuming **CP as 100** simplifies calculations involving percentages and ratios.

questions.question: If the median of a data is 45.98 less than its mode, then the median of the data exceeds its mean by _____. (Use empirical formula)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Empirical Relationship** between central tendencies is: **(Mode − Median) = 2 × (Median − Mean)**.

Given that **Median** is 45.98 less than **Mode**, we have: **Mode − Median = 45.98**.

Applying the trick: 45.98 = 2 × (Median − Mean).

Required value = 45.98 ÷ 2 = 22.99.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.99.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between **Mode** and **Median** = 45.98

**Formula Used:**

**Empirical Formula:** Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0844e395c8720a7ca75b75b6d324ae49949ecfc5c16cad7b5727a88cda9b31f8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

Subtract **Median** from both sides:

⇒ Mode − Median = (3 × Median − 2 × Mean) − Median

⇒ Mode − Median = 2 × Median − 2 × Mean

⇒ Mode − Median = 2 × (Median − Mean)

Substitute the given value (Mode − Median = 45.98):

⇒ 45.98 = 2 × (Median − Mean)

⇒ Median − Mean = 45.98 ÷ 2

⇒ Median − Mean = 22.99

**∴ The correct answer is 22.99.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**. This is also expressed as **Mean − Mode = 3(Mean − Median)**.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution** (like a Normal Distribution), the values of **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Skewness and Central Tendency

In a **positively skewed** distribution, Mean > Median > Mode. In a **negatively skewed** distribution, Mode > Median > Mean.</p

questions.question: The average of eight numbers is 14. The average of five of these numbers is 14. The average of the remaining three numbers is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If the **Average** of a subset (5 numbers) is equal to the overall **Average** (14), the **Average** of the remaining numbers must also be the same.

Net deviation from the **Mean** must be 0.

Since 5 numbers contribute 0 deviation (14 − 14 = 0), the **remaining 3 numbers** must also have a net deviation of 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Total numbers** = 8 | **Total Average** = 14

**First subset** = 5 numbers | **Subset Average** = 14

**Formula Used:**

Sum = Average × Count

Average of remaining = (Total Sum − Subset Sum) ÷ Remaining Count

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d1a83ef627b51cec0713f2480e80ebe0861a4a78814e2440b3135e09ef0eefd.png] 

⇒ **Total Sum** = 8 × 14 = 112

⇒ **Sum of 5 numbers** = 5 × 14 = 70

⇒ **Sum of remaining 3 numbers** = 112 − 70 = 42

⇒ **Average of remaining 3 numbers** = 42 ÷ 3 = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

**__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

The arithmetic mean or average is calculated as the Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Rule

The sum of deviations of all values in a data set from their **arithmetic mean** is always equal to **zero**.</p

questions.question: A local train without stoppages runs at an average speed of 70 km/hr, and with stoppages, at an average speed of 30 km/hr. What is the total time (in hours) taken by the local train for stoppages on a route of length 630 km?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Time for stoppages per hour = (Fast Speed − Slow Speed) ÷ Fast Speed

Stoppage time per hour = (70 − 30) ÷ 70 = 40/70 = 4/7 hours

Total time with stoppages = Total Distance ÷ Speed with stoppages = 630 ÷ 30 = 21 hours

Total stoppage time = 21 × (4/7) = 12 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average speed **without stoppages** = 70 km/hr

Average speed **with stoppages** = 30 km/hr

**Total distance** of the route = 630 km
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a524e0cdf32f87b21bb61a71b19f69600ad962e6a8c632e16de1ee33380566c0.png] 
**Calculations:**

⇒ Actual travel time (without stoppages) = Distance ÷ Speed without stoppages

⇒ Travel time = 630 ÷ 70 = 9 hours

⇒ Total time taken (with stoppages) = Distance ÷ Speed with stoppages

⇒ Total time = 630 ÷ 30 = 21 hours

⇒ Stoppage time = Total time − Actual travel time

⇒ Stoppage time = 21 − 9 = 12 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Concept

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. Stoppages increase the total time, thereby reducing the average speed.

Stoppage Time Formula

Stoppage time per hour = (Difference in Speeds) ÷ (Faster Speed). To find total stoppage time, multiply this by the total time taken with stoppages.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, it is S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: The ratio between the perimeter and breadth of a rectangle is 3 : 1. If the area of the rectangle is 98 cm², find the perimeter (in cm) of the rectangle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Perimeter** (2(L+B)) to **Breadth** (B) is 3 : 1.

⇒ 2L + 2B = 3B ⇒ 2L = B

Since Area = L × B = 98 ⇒ L × 2L = 98 ⇒ 2L² = 98 ⇒ L² = 49 ⇒ L = 7 cm.

Then B = 2 × 7 = 14 cm.

questions.question: The ratio of the lengths of two corresponding sides of two similar triangles is 10 : 9. The ratio of the areas of these two triangles, in the order mentioned, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any two **similar triangles**, the ratio of their **areas** is equal to the **square** of the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

Ratio of corresponding sides = 10 : 9

⇒ Ratio of areas = 10² : 9²

⇒ Ratio of areas = 100 : 81

**∴ The correct answer is 100 : 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of the lengths of two **corresponding sides** of two **similar triangles** = 10 : 9

**Formula Used:**

If ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR, then:

Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔPQR) = (AB / PQ)² = (BC / QR)² = (AC / PR)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea3ba7417e32f72dfa9573167b4ce0fa4ff486f71d8be2f1b78860cab6765591.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **corresponding sides** of the two triangles be s₁ and s₂.

⇒ s₁ / s₂ = 10 / 9

Let the **areas** of the two triangles be A₁ and A₂.

According to the **Area of Similar Triangles Theorem**:

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = (s₁ / s₂)²

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = (10 / 9)²

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = (10 × 10) / (9 × 9)

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = 100 / 81

⇒ A₁ : A₂ = 100 : 81

**∴ The correct answer is 100 : 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Perimeters

For two **similar triangles**, the ratio of their **perimeters** is equal to the ratio of their **corresponding sides** (s₁ : s₂).

Ratio of Altitudes and Medians

The ratio of **corresponding altitudes**, **medians**, or **angle bisectors** of two **similar triangles** is also equal to the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

Conditions for Similarity

Two triangles are **similar** if their **corresponding angles** are equal (AAA) or their **corresponding sides** are in the same ratio (SSS or SAS).</p

questions.question: M is inversely proportional to N. If M is 18, then N is 21. If N = 27, then what is the value of M?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
For **inversely proportional** quantities, the product of variables remains **constant**: M₁ × N₁ = M₂ × N₂.

Initial product: 18 × 21 = 378

New product: M × 27 = 378

M = 378 ÷ 27 = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e27849a877dbb322f6e628299816c6e6cd96e3f2cd528a3c1ba2500ffdbad1ed.png] 
**Given:** M is **inversely proportional** to N. M₁ = 18, N₁ = 21, N₂ = 27.

**Formula Used:** M = k/N or M × N = k (where k is a **constant**).

⇒ 18 × 21 = k

⇒ k = 378

⇒ Now, M₂ × N₂ = 378

⇒ M₂ × 27 = 378

⇒ M₂ = 378 ÷ 27

⇒ M₂ = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

In **direct proportion**, the ratio of variables is constant: y/x = k or y₁/x₁ = y₂/x₂.

Inverse Proportion Property

If one quantity increases, the other **decreases** proportionally such that their product remains the **same**.

Proportionality Constant

The value k = M × N is known as the **constant of proportionality** for inverse variation.</p

questions.question: What major tax reform was introduced by the 101st Amendment Act, 2016?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax (GST)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India through the **101st Amendment Act, 2016**.
 
• It was implemented on **July 1, 2017**, replacing multiple indirect taxes like service tax, VAT, and excise duty.
 
• GST is a **destination-based tax**, meaning it is levied at the point of consumption rather than the point of origin.
 
• The tax structure includes four main slabs: **0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%**, depending on the type of goods and services.
 
• GST is governed by a dual structure, where both the Central Government (CGST) and State Governments (SGST) collect taxes on intra-state transactions, while inter-state transactions attract Integrated GST (IGST).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Input Tax Credit (ITC):**

 
 
• Under GST, businesses can claim credit for taxes paid on purchases as a set-off against taxes payable on sales.
 
• This eliminates the cascading effect of taxes, making the tax system more efficient.
 
 
 
• **GST Council:**
 
 
• The GST Council is a constitutional body chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
 
• It consists of representatives from both the Central and State Governments to decide GST rates, policies, and reforms.
 
 
 
• **Types of GST:**
 
 
• **CGST:** Central Goods and Services Tax, levied by the central government.
 
• **SGST:** State Goods and Services Tax, levied by state governments.
 
• **IGST:** Integrated Goods and Services Tax, applicable on inter-state transactions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of GST:**
 
 
• GST has simplified the tax structure in India by consolidating multiple indirect taxes.
 
• It has improved tax compliance and brought transparency to the taxation system.
 
• It has boosted India's ease of doing business rankings by streamlining tax processes for businesses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **Pressure** is defined as the **force** applied per unit **area**.
 
• Mathematically, **Pressure = Force / Area**.
 
• **Force** has the dimensional formula **[MLT⁻²]**, where M = mass, L = length, T = time.
 
• **Area** has the dimensional formula **[L2]**.
 
• Dividing force by area gives **[MLT⁻²] / [L²] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²]**, which is the dimensional formula of pressure.
 
• **Applications:** Pressure is used in fields like **fluid mechanics, hydraulics, meteorology, and engineering design**.
 
• **Examples:** Atmospheric pressure, blood pressure, and pressure in hydraulic lifts.

 __
 
• **Surface tension** represents force per unit **length** along the surface of a liquid.
 
• Common applications include **capillary action, formation of droplets, and liquid interfaces in engineering.**
 
 
 
• **[ML²T⁻²]**__: This represents **moment of force or torque**.
 __
 
• It is calculated as **Force × Distance** from the pivot.
 
• Used in applications such as **lever systems, mechanical rotation, and structural analysis.**
 
 
 
• **[MLT⁻²]**__: This is the dimensional formula for force itself.
 
 
• **Force** acts on objects to produce **acceleration**.
 
• Applications include **mechanics, dynamics, and structural design calculations.**

questions.question: At what rate of interest per annum will a sum of ₹15,625 amount to ₹19,683 in 1 year and 6 months, if the interest is compounded half-yearly?

For **compounded half-yearly**, time **1 year 6 months** = **3** half-year cycles.

Ratio of **Amount** to **Principal** for 3 cycles = 19,683 ÷ 15,625 = (27/25)³.

Rate per half-year = [(27 − 25) / 25] × 100 = 8%.

Annual **Rate of Interest** = 8% × 2 = 16%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Principal (P)** = ₹15,625, **Amount (A)** = ₹19,683, **Time (T)** = 1.5 years.

**Formula Used:** A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where **r** is the rate per period and **n** is the number of periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8935df6315d1d664b3c0502a66a87c7bdeea00a426d6af4bf80220186a32586d.png] 

⇒ Total periods (n) = 1.5 years × 2 = 3 periods.

⇒ 19,683 = 15,625 × (1 + r/100)³

⇒ 19,683 / 15,625 = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ (27/25)³ = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ 1 + r/100 = 27/25

⇒ r/100 = 27/25 − 1 = 2/25

⇒ r = (2/25) × 100 = 8% per half-year.

⇒ Annual Rate = 8% × 2 = 16%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is **compounded half-yearly**, the annual rate is halved (R/2) and the time is doubled (2 × T).

Quarterly Compounding

When interest is **compounded quarterly**, the annual rate is divided by 4 (R/4) and the time is multiplied by 4 (4 × T).

Effective Rate of Interest

It is the actual annual interest rate when compounding occurs more than once a year, calculated as [(1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1] × 100.

questions.question: The mention of DNA as a long polymer of deoxyribonucleotides implies which structural characteristic?

options.text: It is composed of a sugar-phosphate backbone and nitrogenous bases.
Each nucleotide is linked by hydrogen bonds in a parallel fashion.
The molecule consists of multiple independent short chains.
The sequence is circular and self-replicating.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is composed of a sugar-phosphate backbone and nitrogenous bases.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is a long polymer composed of repeating units called **deoxyribonucleotides**, which form the basic structural framework.
 
• Each nucleotide in DNA consists of three components: a **deoxyribose sugar**, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base.
 
• The sugar-phosphate backbone forms the structural framework, while the nitrogenous bases project inward, forming complementary base pairs.
 
• The nitrogenous bases include **adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), and guanine (G)**, which pair specifically (A with T and C with G) through hydrogen bonding.
 
• This arrangement results in the characteristic **double-helix structure** of DNA, with the sugar-phosphate backbone on the outside and base pairs on the inside.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nucleotides:** The building blocks of DNA, composed of a nitrogenous base, a deoxyribose sugar, and a phosphate group.
 
• **Complementary Base Pairing:** Adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds, while cytosine pairs with guanine through three hydrogen bonds, ensuring the stability of the double helix.
 
• **Sugar-Phosphate Backbone:** This backbone provides structural integrity and is formed through phosphodiester bonds between the 5' phosphate group of one nucleotide and the 3' hydroxyl group of the adjacent nucleotide.
 
• **Double-Helix Model:** Proposed by Watson and Crick in 1953, the DNA double helix consists of two antiparallel strands twisted around each other.
 
• **Central Dogma of Molecular Biology:** DNA serves as the template for RNA synthesis (transcription), which in turn guides protein synthesis (translation), highlighting its critical role in genetic information storage and expression.

questions.question: Find a single discount (rounded up to two decimal places) equal to three consecutive discounts of 3%, 27% and 23%.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net discount for **3%** and **27%** = 3 + 27 − (3 × 27) ÷ 100 = 30 − 0.81 = **29.19%**.

Now, combine **29.19%** and **23%** = 29.19 + 23 − (29.19 × 23) ÷ 100.

= 52.19 − (671.37 ÷ 100) = 52.19 − 6.7137 = **45.4763%**.

Rounding up to two decimal places, we get **45.48%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.48%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Three successive discounts: **d₁ = 3%**, **d₂ = 27%**, **d₃ = 23%**.
Formulas: **Successive Discount = a + b − (ab ÷ 100)** | **Final SP = MP × (100−d₁)/100 × (100−d₂)/100 × (100−d₃)/100**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/899c77588cdada243bbbb2c924f3886c0a0bcaa35db0a18189fc08dbe3e46118.png] 
⇒ Let the **Marked Price (MP)** be 100.
⇒ After 1st discount: 100 × (97 ÷ 100) = 97.
⇒ After 2ⁿd discount: 97 × (73 ÷ 100) = 70.81.
⇒ After 3rd discount: 70.81 × (77 ÷ 100) = 54.5237.
⇒ Total Discount = MP − Final SP = 100 − 54.5237 = **45.4763%**.
⇒ Rounding to 2 decimal places ≈ **45.48%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.48%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are applied one after another on the reduced price, they are called successive discounts. The order of application does not change the final result.

Single Equivalent Discount Formula

For three discounts d₁, d₂, and d₃, the equivalent discount is 1 − [(1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) × (1 − d₃/100)] × 100%.</p

• The concept of Akam is complemented by **Puram**, which deals with external aspects like war, heroism, and public life.

questions.question: A vendor sells oranges at ₹44 each and incurs a loss of 78%. If he wants to make a profit of 78%, at what price (in ₹) should he sell each orange?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100%.

Initial **Selling Price (SP₁)** at 78% loss = 100% − 78% = 22%.

Required **Selling Price (SP₂)** for 78% profit = 100% + 78% = 178%.

Given: 22% ⇒ ₹44. Since 22 × 2 = 44, the multiplier is 2.

Required SP₂ = 178% × 2 = ₹356.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹356.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP₁ = ₹44, Loss₁ = 78%, Profit₂ = 78%.

**Formulas:** CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%); New SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d33628492a0dd4c476d4c16df124b034a80340a6b3e542c071078b0109545a37.png] 

⇒ CP = 44 × 100 ÷ (100 − 78) = 44 × 100 ÷ 22

⇒ CP = 2 × 100 = **₹200**.

⇒ New SP = 200 × (100 + 78) ÷ 100

⇒ New SP = 200 × 178 ÷ 100 = 2 × 178

⇒ New SP = **₹356**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹356.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between SP and CP

When the **Cost Price** is constant, the ratio of two different Selling Prices is equal to the ratio of their respective percentage values: SP₁ ÷ (100 − L%) = SP₂ ÷ (100 + P%).

Profit and Loss Percentage

Always calculate **Profit%** or **Loss%** on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise in the question.

questions.question: What is the advantage of keeping food in an airtight container?

It enhances the taste of the food.

__
 
• Storing food in an airtight container limits the exposure of food to **oxygen**, thereby slowing the process of oxidation.
 
• Oxidation is a chemical reaction where food reacts with oxygen, causing spoilage, changes in texture, taste, and nutritional value.
 
• Airtight containers help in reducing the growth of microorganisms, such as molds and aerobic bacteria, that thrive in the presence of oxygen.
 
• By preventing moisture from entering, airtight containers protect food from becoming stale or soggy.
 
• This method is particularly beneficial for preserving the freshness of dry goods, snacks, and perishable items for longer durations.

• It involves the loss of electrons in food molecules caused by oxygen exposure.
 
• This process leads to rancidity in fats, browning of fruits, and degradation of vitamins.
 
 
 
• **Aerobic vs. Anaerobic Bacteria:**
 
 
• Aerobic bacteria require oxygen to grow, while anaerobic bacteria thrive in oxygen-free environments.
 
• Airtight containers reduce aerobic bacterial growth but do not promote anaerobic bacterial growth unless improperly sealed.
 
 
 
• **Materials Used in Airtight Containers:**
 
 
• Containers are typically made of plastic, glass, or metal with silicone or rubber seals to ensure airtightness.
 
• Proper sealing prevents air and moisture from entering, maintaining food quality.
 
 
 
• **Storage Tips:**
 
 
• Foods with high moisture content should also be kept in airtight containers to avoid mold formation.
 
• Dry goods like grains, cereals, and snacks last longer when stored in airtight conditions.
 
 
 
• **Preservation Techniques:**
 
 
• Airtight storage complements other preservation methods such as refrigeration and freezing.
 
• It is also widely used in vacuum-sealing techniques to extend shelf life.

questions.question: When appointing Governors of States and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories, the President of India acts on the advice of which body?
questions.solution:

• This is in accordance with the principle of the parliamentary system, where the President acts on the advice of the executive body.
 
• The Union Council of Ministers is responsible for aiding and advising the President in exercising their constitutional powers.
 
• Article **74(1)** of the Indian Constitution mandates that the President shall act in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• Governors serve as the constitutional head of the state, and their appointment is a part of the President's discretionary powers, executed in consultation with the executive.

• **Governor's Role:**
 
 
• The Governor acts as the constitutional head of the state and ensures that the state government functions within the framework of the Constitution.
 
• They are responsible for summoning and proroguing the state legislature, appointing the Chief Minister, and giving assent to state bills.
 
 
 
• **Lieutenant Governor:**
 
 
• The Lieutenant Governor is the administrative head of Union Territories like Delhi, Puducherry, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• They exercise powers delegated to them by the President of India under various provisions of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 74 of the Constitution:**

questions.question: The length of a rectangular plot is (x² + xy + y²) m and its breadth is (x2 - 5xy - y2) m. Find its perimeter, when x = 1 and y = - 1.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put the values of **x = 1** and **y = −1** directly into the expressions for length (L) and breadth (B).

L = 1² + 1(−1) + (−1)² = 1 − 1 + 1 = 1 m.

B = 1² − 5(1)(−1) − (−1)² = 1 + 5 − 1 = 5 m.

Perimeter = 2(L + B) = 2(1 + 5) = 2 × 6 = 12 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71bbe0a0a20fef1ea7d7ded70f9668622296d27c79770cab70672adc0a2c9f13.png] 

**Given:**

Length (L) = x² + xy + y²

Breadth (B) = x² − 5xy − y²

Values: **x = 1**, **y = −1**

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of Rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

**Calculations:**

⇒ L = (1)² + (1)(−1) + (−1)²

⇒ L = 1 − 1 + 1 = 1 m

⇒ B = (1)² − 5(1)(−1) − (−1)²

⇒ B = 1 + 5 − 1 = 5 m

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (1 + 5)

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × 6 = 12 m

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total space occupied by the rectangle, calculated as Area = Length × Breadth.

Diagonal of Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners, given by d = √(L² + B²).

Algebraic Substitution

Always substitute negative values within parentheses to ensure correct sign application (e.g., (−1)² = 1).</p

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 2 : 14 : 3, and their LCM is 4116. Their HCF is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **HCF** of the numbers be **H**.

Numbers are 2H, 14H, and 3H.

**LCM** of (2, 14, 3) × **H** = 4116

42 × **H** = 4116 ⇒ **H** = 4116 ÷ 42 = 98.

**∴ The correct answer is 98.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of numbers = 2 : 14 : 3

**LCM** = 4116

**Formula Used:**

If numbers are ax, bx, and cx (where x is **HCF**), then **LCM** = **LCM**(a, b, c) × x.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a70b9a8eaa600fde1aea1ba66e06989687ddeeff7c4d9f37db0725649f990a49.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the numbers be 2x, 14x, and 3x.

⇒ **LCM** of (2x, 14x, 3x) = 4116

⇒ To find **LCM** of 2, 14, and 3:

⇒ 2 = 2¹, 14 = 2 × 7, 3 = 3¹

⇒ **LCM** = 2 × 7 × 3 = 42

⇒ Therefore, **LCM**(2x, 14x, 3x) = 42x

⇒ 42x = 4116

⇒ x = 4116 ÷ 42

⇒ x = 98

**∴ The correct answer is 98.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Relation

For two numbers A and B, **Product of numbers** = **HCF** × **LCM**. This rule does not directly apply to more than two numbers.

Co-prime Numbers

If the numbers in a ratio are **co-prime**, then their **LCM** is simply the product of the numbers and their **HCF**.

HCF Properties

**HCF** is always a **factor** of the **LCM** for any given set of numbers.</p

questions.question: Income of Amit in 2019 was ₹22,000. He gets an increment of 20% every year. What was his income (in ₹) in 2021?

questions.question: 7 times the present age of X is 6 years less than 2 times the present age of Y. At present, P is 7 times as old as X, and Y is 6 years younger than Q. If P is 70 years older than Q, then the present age (in years) of Y is :

From given data, **P = 7X** and **P = Q + 70** ⇒ **7X = Q + 70**.

Since **Q = Y + 6**, substitute: **7X = (Y + 6) + 70 = Y + 76**.

Given equation: **7X = 2Y − 6**.

Equating both: **Y + 76 = 2Y − 6** ⇒ **Y = 82**.

**∴ The correct answer is 82 years.**

4) **P = Q + 70**

Substitute (2) and (3) into (4):

⇒ **7X = (Y + 6) + 70**

⇒ **7X = Y + 76**

⇒ **2Y − 6 = Y + 76**

questions.question: The mean proportional between (21 + 16sqrt{2}) and (16 - 7sqrt{2}) is :

The **mean proportional** between two numbers **a** and **b** is given by the formula **√(a × b)**.

Multiply (21 + 16√2) and (16 − 7√2) directly using FOIL method.

Product = (21 × 16) − (21 × 7√2) + (16√2 × 16) − (16√2 × 7√2) = 336 − 147√2 + 256√2 − 224.

Simplified Product = 112 + 109√2.

**∴ The correct answer is √(112 + 109√2).**

⇒ Mean Proportional = √[336 − 147√2 + 256√2 − 224]

⇒ Mean Proportional = √[(336 − 224) + (256 − 147)√2]

questions.question: Let ABC and DEF be two triangles such that ∠A = ∠D = 40° and AB = DE. What is the condition required to be met such that ABC and DEF are similar triangles?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two triangles to be **similar**, their corresponding angles must be equal according to the **AA (Angle-Angle) Similarity Criterion**.

Given: ∠A = ∠D = 40°.

To satisfy similarity, we need at least one more pair of **corresponding angles** to be equal.

From the options, **∠C = ∠F** provides the necessary second pair of equal corresponding angles.

Since ∠A = ∠D and ∠C = ∠F, the triangles **ΔABC** and **ΔDEF** are similar by **AA similarity**.

**∴ The correct answer is ∠C = ∠F.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** In ΔABC and ΔDEF, ∠A = ∠D = 40° and AB = DE.

**Formula Used:** **AA Similarity Criterion** — If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another triangle, then the triangles are similar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c0bfacfb0bc7286d060fe586757976d96fd52130c04692afe71670144cbfcb0.png] 

To prove ΔABC ~ ΔDEF:

⇒ We already have one pair of equal angles: ∠A = ∠D = 40°.

⇒ According to the **AA Similarity Criterion**, we need another pair of corresponding angles to be equal.

⇒ The corresponding vertices are A → D, B → E, and C → F.

⇒ Therefore, either **∠B = ∠E** or **∠C = ∠F** must be true.

⇒ Checking the options, **∠C = ∠F** is provided in option (1).

⇒ Note: Since AB = DE is also given, if ∠C = ∠F, then ∠B = ∠E (angle sum property), making the triangles **congruent** by **ASA**. Since all congruent triangles are similar, the condition is satisfied.

**∴ The correct answer is ∠C = ∠F.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

AA Similarity Criterion

If two angles of one triangle are respectively equal to two angles of another triangle, then the two triangles are similar.

SAS Similarity Criterion

If one angle of a triangle is equal to one angle of another triangle and the sides including these angles are proportional, then the triangles are similar.

Similarity vs Congruence

Congruent triangles have the same shape and size (ratio of sides = 1), while similar triangles have the same shape but may differ in size (ratio of sides is constant).</p

questions.question: Kanchan’s salary is ₹12,000 per month. He spends ₹4,000 on house rent and ₹2,000 on bills, and the rest of the amount is his monthly savings. Find his savings (in ₹) in a year, if in the month of his birthday, he spent all his monthly savings on birthday celebrations.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Monthly Savings** = 12,000 − (4,000 + 2,000) = ₹6,000.

In his **birthday month**, savings = ₹0.

Total Savings in a year = 6,000 × 11 months = ₹66,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹66,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ **Monthly Savings** = 12,000 − (4,000 + 2,000) = ₹6,000

⇒ **Total months** in a year = 12

⇒ Savings is 0 for **1 month** (Birthday month)

⇒ **Total Annual Savings** = 6,000 × (12 − 1)

⇒ **Total Annual Savings** = 6,000 × 11 = ₹66,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹66,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure and Savings

Percentage Savings

Savings Percentage = (Savings ÷ Total Income) × 100. In this case, monthly savings % = (6,000 ÷ 12,000) × 100 = 50%.

Annual Calculations

Always account for specific monthly variations (like bonuses or one-time expenses) by multiplying the regular monthly value by (12 − number of variation months).

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 87?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number 87 = 3 × 29. A number divisible by 87 must be divisible by both **3** and **29**.

Checking divisibility by 3: Sum of digits of 7221 = 7 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 12 (Divisible by 3).

Checking 7221 ÷ 87: 87 × 80 = 6960. Remainder = 7221 − 6960 = 261.

87 × 3 = 261. So, 7221 is exactly divisible by 87.

**∴ The correct answer is 7221.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number 87 and four options.

**Method:** Perform **direct division** for each option to find the number with remainder 0.

⇒ Option 1: 7221 ÷ 87

⇒ 87 × 8 = 696

⇒ 722 − 696 = 26

⇒ Bring down 1 → 261

⇒ 87 × 3 = 261

⇒ Remainder = 0. So, 7221 is divisible.

⇒ Option 2: 7099 ÷ 87 → 7099 = 87 × 81 + 52 (Not divisible)

⇒ Option 3: 6712 ÷ 87 → 6712 = 87 × 77 + 13 (Not divisible)

⇒ Option 4: 7741 ÷ 87 → 7741 = 87 × 88 + 85 (Not divisible)

**∴ The correct answer is 7221.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of 3.

Composite Number Divisibility

If a number is divisible by two **co-prime** numbers a and b, it is also divisible by their product (a × b).

Divisibility Rule of 29

Add 3 times the last digit to the remaining number. If the result is divisible by 29, the original number is also divisible.</p

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 9 km/hr and the speed of the stream is 5 km/hr. A man rows to a place at a distance of 75.6 km and comes back to the starting point. Find the total time (in hours) taken by him.

**Downstream Speed** (D) = 9 + 5 = 14 km/hr

**Upstream Speed** (U) = 9 − 5 = 4 km/hr

Total Time = Distance × (1/D + 1/U) = 75.6 × (1/14 + 1/4)

Total Time = 75.6 × (18/56) = 24.3 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 24.3 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed (Sd) = x + y

Upstream Speed (Sᵤ) = x − y

⇒ Upstream Speed = 9 − 5 = 4 km/hr

⇒ Downstream Time (t₁) = 75.6 ÷ 14 = 5.4 hours

⇒ Upstream Time (t₂) = 75.6 ÷ 4 = 18.9 hours

Still Water Speed Formula

Speed of boat in still water = (Downstream speed + Upstream speed) ÷ 2

Stream Speed Formula

Speed of current/stream = (Downstream speed − Upstream speed) ÷ 2

Average Speed in Boats and Streams

questions.question: If α, β and γ are the roots of the equation 6x³ − 11x² + 6x − 1 = 0, find Σα²βγ.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the symmetric property: Σα²βγ = αβγ(α + β + γ).

From the equation 6x³ − 11x² + 6x − 1 = 0, find the **sum of roots** and **product of roots**.

Sum (α + β + γ) = −(−11)/6 = 11/6 and Product (αβγ) = −(−1)/6 = 1/6.

Required value = (1/6) × (11/6) = 11/36.

**∴ The correct answer is 11/36.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The cubic equation is 6x³ − 11x² + 6x − 1 = 0 with roots α, β, and γ.

**Formula Used:** For a cubic equation ax³ + bx² + cx + d = 0:

Sum of roots (α + β + γ) = −b/a

Product of roots (αβγ) = −d/a

⇒ a = 6, b = −11, c = 6, d = −1

⇒ α + β + γ = −(−11)/6 = 11/6

⇒ αβγ = −(−1)/6 = 1/6

⇒ The expression Σα²βγ = α²βγ + αβ²γ + αβγ²

⇒ Taking αβγ common: Σα²βγ = αβγ(α + β + γ)

⇒ Value = (1/6) × (11/6)

⇒ Value = 11/36

**∴ The correct answer is 11/36.**

**__Additional Information__**

Vieta's Formulas (Cubic)

For ax³ + bx² + cx + d = 0, Σα = −b/a, Σαβ = c/a, and αβγ = −d/a.

Symmetric Functions of Roots

Functions like Σα² = (Σα)² − 2(Σαβ) are invariant under any permutation of the roots.

Sum of Squares Formula

α² + β² + γ² = (α + β + γ)² − 2(αβ + βγ + γα).</p

questions.question: In which year did the English East India Company pass a new law that required every new person who took up employment in the Company’s army to serve overseas if required?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1856**__.

• In **1856**, the English East India Company passed a law mandating that soldiers employed in its army had to serve overseas if required.
 
• This law was significant as it challenged the traditional beliefs of Indian sepoys, particularly regarding crossing the seas, which was considered against their religious practices.
 
• The resentment caused by this law among Indian soldiers contributed to the growing unrest that eventually culminated in the **Revolt of 1857**.
 
• This regulation was part of the larger socio-political changes introduced by the British to consolidate their control over India.
 
• The law showcased the disregard of the British towards local cultural sensitivities, leading to widespread dissatisfaction among Indian troops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is considered the first major uprising against British rule in India.
 
• Both sepoys and civilians participated in the revolt, which started in Meerut and spread across northern and central India.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Sensitivities:**
 
 
• Crossing the seas was considered a religious taboo among certain Indian communities, as it was believed to result in the loss of caste.
 
• The imposition of the overseas service regulation was seen as an affront to traditional values.
 
 
 
• **English East India Company:**
 
 
• The company governed India until 1858, after which control was transferred to the British Crown.
 
• Its policies often ignored local customs, leading to widespread dissatisfaction and resistance among Indians.
 
 
 
• **Military Reforms:**
 
 
• British reforms in the Indian army aimed at aligning the forces with Western military practices.
 
• These reforms were often resisted by Indian soldiers due to cultural and religious differences.

questions.question: An electric pump can fill a tank in 3 hours. Due to a leakage in the tank, it takes 5 (1/4) hours to fill the tank. How much time will this leak take to empty the full tank if water does not get in or out of the tank through any other point during this period?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let filling time **A = 3 hours** and combined time (filling + leak) **B = 21/4 hours**.

Leak empty time = (A × B) ÷ (B − A)

⇒ (3 × 21/4) ÷ (21/4 − 3) = (63/4) ÷ (9/4) = 63 ÷ 9 = 7 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time = 3 hr, Filling + Leakage time = 5(1/4) hr = 21/4 hr.

 
 **Entity** **Time (hr)** **Total Work (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 **Pump (P)** 3 21 7 
 **Pump + Leak (P+L)** 21/4 4 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **Pump (P)** = 7 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of **Pump + Leak (P+L)** = 4 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of **Leak (L)** = (P+L) − P = 4 − 7 = −3 units/hr (Negative sign indicates emptying)

⇒ Time taken by **Leak** to empty the tank = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Leak

⇒ Time = 21 ÷ 3 = 7 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An **Inlet** fills a tank (positive efficiency), while an **Outlet or Leak** empties it (negative efficiency).

Combined Work Formula

If pipe A fills in 'x' hours and pipe B empties in 'y' hours, the net work done in one hour is (1/x − 1/y).

Emptying Time Calculation

Time to empty = (Filling Time × Combined Time) ÷ (Combined Time − Filling Time).</p

questions.question: A factory produces 15, 20, 25, 10, and 30 units of a gadget over five days. What is the average production (in units) per day?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total units produced = 15 + 20 + 25 + 10 + 30 = 100 units.

Number of days = 5.

Average = Total Production ÷ Total Days = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Production values for 5 days: 15, 20, 25, 10, and 30 **units**.

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a41afba47b110e1944445e82556b4af17d60db867adee69c7f8cdaa4366f7528.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = 15 + 20 + 25 + 10 + 30

⇒ Sum = 100 **units**

⇒ Total Number of Days = 5

⇒ Average = 100 ÷ 5

⇒ Average = 20 **units**

**∴ The correct answer is 20 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When items have different weights, the average is calculated as Σ(wᵢxᵢ) ÷ Σwᵢ.

Deviation Method

The sum of the **deviations** of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero.

Average of AP

For a series in **Arithmetic Progression**, the average is simply (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.</p
